Open Start and type your shop name and your own limits in the yellow cells: margin before ads, target return, discount cap, open rate target and the days before a customer is lapsed.
Check Channels, Team, Products and Discount Codes: the other pages pick channels, people, SKUs and codes from them.
List your ad campaigns on Ad Campaigns with a daily budget and a target return, then type one row for each campaign and week on Ad Lines.
Plan the spend for each month and channel on Ad Budget Plan and read the variance and the check next to it.
Put every promotion on Marketing Calendar with dates, code, budget and goal, and read the margin check before you launch.
After a promotion ends, enter its orders, revenue, discount and cost of goods on Promotion Results and read the margin after ads and the uplift.
Enter your e-mail sends on E-mail Sends and the month figures on E-mail List; Segments holds the rules of your groups.
Plan content on Content Calendar, creator posts on Creator Posts, and sponsored listings on Sponsored Listings.
Fix listing problems on Product Feed Quality and keep the peaks on Seasonal Plan.
Read Monthly Marketing for cost per new customer and repeat rate, and Win-back List for customers who stopped ordering.

Use the 14 calculators for return, cost per order, budget split, discount cost, uplift, code check, campaign result, e-mail value, list growth, customer value, creator value, shipping offers, peak budget and what-if.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to send 28 ready texts.
Read Marketing Dashboard and Charts every week.
See which channel, product and customer really earn money
Channel profit, payouts, products, customers and wholesale
fees, shipping, ads, returns, packaging and picking labour come off each channel and month, and the margin is checked against your goal and floor
every payout is compared with the expected net after fees, refunds and ad fees, and marked matching, short or overpaid
short payments are followed to the money recovered, with days open and the amount still to claim
commission, payment and monthly fees of each channel sit in one table that the calculators and the profit sheet read
products are ranked by revenue with a running share and an A, B or C class, so you see which few lines carry the shop
stock cover, cash tied up and a planned action are shown for products that stopped selling
the usual gap between orders gives the date a customer should order again and flags those who stopped
open and overdue invoices are set against the credit limit and terms of each account
customers are grouped by their first month and followed to see how many order again
sales less goods, stall fee and labour give the result of each day and per hour, with a grade
views, carts and orders of each listing give conversion rates and a flag for listings to fix or push

One row for each channel and fee element: commission, payment fee, fixed fee, monthly fee, shipping rule, payout rhythm and return window; the cost of each fee on a typical order fills in by itself.
One row for each month and channel with orders, units, revenue, discounts and shipping charged; average order value, profit, margin and the share of the month fill in by themselves.
Channel profit after fees, shipping, ads and returns
One row for each month and channel with the costs of selling; handling, shipping net, profit, margin, fee share, return on ads and a check against the channel goal fill in by themselves.
Payouts from the channels and what they should have been
One row for each payout with gross sales, fees, refunds, ad fees and the amount paid; the expected net, the difference, the check and the days to payout fill in by themselves.
Payout differences: cause, claim and money recovered
One row for each payout that was paid short or too much with the cause, the claim and what came back; the channel, the shortfall, what is left to claim and the days open fill in by themselves.
Product ranking: revenue, margin, returns and ABC class
One row for each product with its history of units and revenue; margin, return rate, rank, share of revenue, cumulative share and ABC class fill in by themselves. Tag the ten best and ten weakest.
One row for each product and channel that sold it with units and revenue; the product, the category, the average price and the share of the product revenue on that channel fill in by themselves.
Slow and unprofitable products with an action
One row for each product under review with the action you chose; units, last sale, stock cover, margin, cash tied up and the problem fill in by themselves.
Customers: wholesale accounts and repeat buyers
One row for each wholesale account and repeat retail customer with kind, region, tier, terms, credit limit and discount; other retail customers are counted in the sheets New and Repeat and Cohorts.
Customer orders summary: who orders, how often and who is
One row for each customer with orders, revenue, first and last order; days since the last order, the usual gap between orders and the status (new, active, at risk, lapsed) fill in by themselves.
New and repeat customers by month
One row for each month with new and repeat customers, their orders and revenue; the repeat share of orders, the repeat share of revenue and the change in new customers fill in by themselves.
Customer cohorts: how many still order
One row for each first-order month and month since: the customers in the cohort and how many ordered again; the retention share and the customers lost fill in by themselves.
Wholesale account book: tier, terms, credit and what is owed
One row for each wholesale account with tier, terms, credit limit, discount, owner and review date; revenue, orders, open and overdue invoices, credit used and days to pay fill in by themselves.
Wholesale invoices: due date, payment and days overdue
One row for each invoice to a wholesale account with the due date and the payment date; the status, the days overdue, the amount still open and the days to pay fill in by themselves.
Wholesale order rhythm: when each account should order next
One row for each wholesale account with its usual gap between orders and its last order; the next expected order, the days to it and a flag (on rhythm, due soon, overdue, stopped) fill in by.
Market stall days: sales, fees and what the day earned
One row for each Saturday market day with sales, units, goods cost, stall fee and hours worked; labour, the result, the result per hour and a grade fill in by themselves.
Regional sales by quarter: orders, shipping and sales tax
One row for each region and quarter with orders, revenue, shipping charged and paid and sales tax collected; shipping net, average order, tax share and the share of the quarter fill in by themselves.
Channel goals: monthly revenue and margin goals against
One row for each month and channel with the revenue goal and the margin goal; the actual revenue, profit and margin, the gap and whether the goal was met fill in by themselves.
Listing performance: views, carts, orders and conversion
One row for each product listing on a channel for the last 30 days with views, carts, orders and revenue; the conversion rate, the cart rate, revenue per view and a check fill in by themselves.
One row for each thing you noticed about rivals, the channels or the market, with its date, channel and effect; keep it short so the quarterly channel plan can use it.
Wholesale accounts at risk or lapsed
Revenue, profit, fees and payouts by month
Product review sheet with its channels
Pick the channel and type a product code and the order details; the fees come from your Channel Fees rules and the cost from Product Ranking. See what the order really earns.

Pick a channel and type your margin and per-order costs; see the order value below which an order loses money and how far a typical order is above it.

Pick the channel and type the payout figures; see the net you should receive, the difference and the likely cause so you can claim it.
Difference as a share of gross sales

Pick the channel and type the totals of a sample of orders; the rule comes from Channel Fees. See whether the fees charged fit the rule and what a gap costs in a year.
Orders per year on this channel
Gap per year if it continues
Product ABC class and share of revenue
Type a product code; the rank, share, cumulative share and class come from Product Ranking. Add a sales change to see how the share would move.
Customer lifetime value and repeat rate
Type the average order, how often a customer buys, your margin and how many stay; see the profit a customer brings over their life and whether it pays back the cost of winning them.

Type how many customers made their first order in a month and how many ordered again in months 1, 2, 3 and 6; see the retention and a view at month 12 against your own average.
Customers lost after the first order
Monthly hold from month 1 to month 6
Customers ordering in month 12 at that pace
Wholesale account value and reorder date
Type the name of a wholesale account as in Customers; see its usual gap between orders, the next expected order, its value per year, profit and what it owes.
Wholesale price tier check: volume against discount
Type a yearly volume and the volume each tier needs; the discounts come from the average of your Customers. See the tier earned, the discount and the margin left after it.
Cost of the discount per year
Profit per year after the discount
Channel mix shift: effect of moving orders
Pick the channel to move orders from and the channel to move them to and the share to move; the profit per order of each channel comes from Channel Profit.
Type the sales, the goods cost share, the stall fee and the hours; see what the day earns after goods, fee, labour and extras, the break-even sales and your average day.
